advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish 'no remote horizon ref' from 'config lookup failed' in `_has_remote_horizon_ref` so a config error does not silently skip the eligibility gate.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:87: `if _has_remote_horizon_ref(tracker) and not _remote_horizon_eligible(`
src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:234-241: `_has_remote_horizon_ref` returns False in the `except (config.ConfigError, OSError, RuntimeError)` branch
Litmus: the 'ref present but config broken' world produces the same False verdict as 'no ref present', so the gate cannot distinguish 'checked and ineligible' from 'check never ran'.
advisory.finding: `_has_remote_horizon_ref` returns False on any config error (`config.ConfigError, OSError, RuntimeError`), and the eligibility gate is only enforced `if _has_remote_horizon_ref(tracker)`. A failed config resolution silently SKIPS the ADR-0106 horizon eligibility check — indistinguishable from a legitimately absent remote-tracking ref — so a collapse can proceed unguarded when config lookup fails.
scenarios: Shadow clone has the remote-tracking horizon ref copied in, but config (remote/branch) resolution raises — eligibility is bypassed and collapse proceeds.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Read commit messages in binary (`text=False`, `--format=%B` with `-z` or `cat-file`) to preserve exact bytes when rewriting.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:330-331: `return _git(tracker, "log", "-1", "--format=%B", commit, input_data=None).stdout.encode()`
Other blob reads deliberately use `text=False` for byte fidelity (e.g. `_tree_entries`, `_blob_bytes_for_entry`), but the message path decodes/re-encodes.
advisory.finding: `_commit_message` reads the commit body with default text mode (`git log --format=%B`, decoded as UTF-8) then re-`.encode()`s it for fast-import. Non-UTF-8 commit messages are lossily decoded/re-encoded, and `git log`'s `%B` output normalization (trailing newline handling) can alter the byte-exact original message, so rewritten commits may not preserve original messages verbatim.
scenarios: A commit with a non-UTF-8 or trailing-whitespace-sensitive message is rewritten through fast-import.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Use `%at %z`/`%ct %z` (or `%ai`/`%ci`) to preserve the original timezone offset instead of forcing +0000.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:316: `fmt = "%an%x00%ae%x00%at +0000%x00%cn%x00%ce%x00%ct +0000"`
`%at`/`%ct` are the raw unix timestamps; the appended ` +0000` overrides the original `%z` offset.
advisory.finding: `_commit_metadata` forces `+0000` onto author/committer dates via `%at +0000` / `%ct +0000`, discarding the original timezone offset. Rewritten commits record UTC offset instead of the original author/committer offset even though the intent is to preserve authorship metadata.
scenarios: Original commits authored in a non-UTC timezone get their recorded offset rewritten to +0000.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a CLI test that runs `rebar reclaim-collapse` against a non-shadow / bad-boundary target and asserts returncode == 2 and the `reclaim-collapse:` stderr message.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:184-186 `except (ReclaimCollapseError, ShadowSafetyError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as exc: print(f"reclaim-collapse: {exc}", file=sys.stderr); return 2`

Named violating input: invoking `rebar reclaim-collapse --shadow-tracker <non-shadow-dir> --boundary <sha>` should exit 2 and print `reclaim-collapse: ...` to stderr, but no test asserts the exit code or stderr message.
tests/unit/test_reclaim_collapse.py:332-356 the sole CLI test (`test_cli_dry_run_reports_plan_without_updating_head`) asserts only `returncode == 0`.

src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py (`_update_current_branch`) `branch = _git(tracker, "symbolic-ref", "-q", "HEAD").stdout.strip(); if not branch: raise ShadowSafetyError("shadow tracker must be on a branch, not detached HEAD")`
Named violating input: `collapse_shadow_tracker(tracker_in_detached_HEAD, boundary_commit=b, apply=True)` should raise ShadowSafetyError('detached HEAD'); no test detaches HEAD before an apply.
ABSENCE: no `detached` case in tests/unit/test_reclaim_collapse.py.
src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:190-194 the text-format `applied`/`dry-run` output branch is only reached from cli(); the sole CLI test uses `--format json` with no `--apply`.
tests/unit/test_reclaim_collapse.py:332-356 CLI test omits `--apply` and uses json format, so the text-output branch and the CLI apply-and-reset path are untested.
advisory.finding: The CLI error path (`return 2` after catching ReclaimCollapseError/ShadowSafetyError/CalledProcessError) is never exercised by any test. All CLI-level coverage is the dry-run happy path.
merged_from: The detached-HEAD ShadowSafetyError in `_update_current_branch` is untested. Applying against a detached HEAD raises 'shadow tracker must be on a branch, not detached HEAD', but no test covers it.

The CLI `--apply` branch is never exercised. The only CLI test uses dry-run; the apply path (which resets HEAD via `_update_current_branch` and prints the 'applied' text form) is only reached via the direct function-level test, not through cli().
scenarios: A regression that made cli() raise instead of returning 2, or swallow errors and return 0, would go undetected.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test passing a boundary that is not an ancestor of the branch tip and asserting ReclaimCollapseError('is not an ancestor').
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:82-83 `if not _is_ancestor(tracker, boundary, original_tip): raise ReclaimCollapseError(f"boundary {boundary} is not an ancestor of {original_tip}")`

Named violating input: calling `collapse_shadow_tracker(tracker, boundary_commit=<a commit not on the branch's history>)` should raise ReclaimCollapseError('... is not an ancestor of ...'); no test asserts this.
ABSENCE: grepping the test file shows no `is not an ancestor` / non-ancestor case.
advisory.finding: The boundary-not-ancestor guard has no test. `collapse_shadow_tracker` raises ReclaimCollapseError when the boundary is not an ancestor of the tip, but no test drives this branch.
scenarios: A regression inverting the `_is_ancestor` check, or removing the guard, would let the engine attempt to collapse across an unrelated commit undetected.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Move `from rebar import config` above the try (or catch ImportError) so the except clause never references an unbound `config`.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:213-222: `from rebar import config` inside try, `except (config.ConfigError, OSError, RuntimeError):`
src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:236-240: same pattern in `_has_remote_horizon_ref`
ImportError is not in the caught tuple and would occur before `config` is bound.
dropped.finding: In `_assert_shadow_tracker` and `_has_remote_horizon_ref` the `except (config.ConfigError, OSError, RuntimeError)` clause references `config`, but `from rebar import config` is imported INSIDE the same `try`. If that import fails (ImportError) the except tuple evaluates `config.ConfigError` on an unbound name, raising `NameError` and masking the original error.
scenarios: Any environment where `rebar.config` import raises during these helpers.
